title: USDS losses flow through a strict waterfall that ends in a haircut to the target price itself
content:
Three provisions in A.3.6 combine into an ordered loss-absorption sequence.

A.3.6.6 sets the seniority: "The SKY Backstop may not be invoked unless the Genesis Capital Backstop... has been applied and USDS remains undercollateralized." Agent-held Genesis Capital is consumed before any SKY is minted, so dilution is a second line of defence, not the first.

A.3.6.5 defines the terminal case: "in case the backstop limit is reached and not overridden, or in case the backstop is halted during the event, the USDS target price receives a haircut to settle the remaining bad debt of the system."

That last clause is the most consequential sentence in the Article. It states, as designed behaviour rather than as failure, that USDS holders are the final loss absorber — the stablecoin's target price is written down to make the system solvent again. A haircut is preferred to leaving unsettled bad debt on the books, which trades the peg's inviolability for the guarantee that the system always closes.

The waterfall is therefore: Genesis Capital, then SKY dilution (subject to a maximum and to a halt mechanism), then the peg. Every discretionary lever in between — the override in A.3.6.3 that permits emission past the maximum, and the halt in A.3.6.4 that stops it early — is really a choice about how much of the loss to push onto SKY holders versus USDS holders.
description: Genesis Capital Backstop must be applied first and USDS still undercollateralized before SKY may be emitted; if emission hits its limit or is halted, the peg absorbs the residual bad debt.
